newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: European bunkers weaken, drawing many buyers back.
newsitem.headline: European bunkers weaken, drawing many buyers back.

text.p: Bunker prices weakened in most European ports, drawing buyers back from their brief abstinence in ARA and parts of the Mediterranean, dealers said.

Rotterdam 380 CST was down $1/$2 a tonne, trading at $125/$126 fob as barges softened. Suppliers said enquiries, very thin earlier this week, multiplied. Many buyers, they said, now acknowledge the high prevailing levels and have learnt to buy on the slight dips. Total ARA volume looked set to be around 15,000 tonnes of fuel oil, with additional good volumes of distillates.
"We've seen a number of enquiries for early November, which is a reasonably healthy sign," one supplier said.
In Hamburg, however, steady prices left German suppliers unable to cash improved European buying.

Mediterranean prices were steady to weak. Spanish demand was healthy. French and Greek ports, which came off $1, also saw a reasonably flow of bunkers, but high Italian prices kept buyers away from Augusta.
Egyptian and Fujairah bunkers came off by $1. Demand in the latter picked up substantially.
Saudi Aramco, meanwhile, raised diesel prices by $5 from October 24, but kept fuel oil prices stable.
